items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-20
items.q: I would work about three nights a week with Al Streeman, and I'd work about three nights a week at the famous store with the late George Girard.

ctx.x: So you'd come back and play a spot with him, even though you would be playing with George Girard.

Right. I would work about three nights a week with Al Streeman, and I'd work about three nights a week at the famous store with the late George Girard. Because I had to get up early in the morning and go to work, and the other bass player who was working with Girard the other three nights, he had to get about three hours sleep and then get up and play with Pinky's Dawn Busters on WWL from 5 to 7 every morning.
Now, who's playing the cowbell there?

items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-15
items.q: And in 53, I went with Gerard and the famous Doe, but I worked there three nights a week and worked with Streaming three nights a week.

ctx.x: How did you get interested in bass by the way?

Well I always did like bass. I always did like string bass, Dick. And around 1937 after playing the guitar for four years in the band I decided, well you know the bass player with the Al Streaming Band who was the vice president of the Soil Company and had to do all that road traveling. He was told Streaming and he said, Al I'm going to have to quit the band. He said, I got too much traveling. He had been with the band ten years. So he left the band and that's when Al told me, he said, Bob why don't you switch…
But why does Treeman want you on bass? Do you know?
